newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower in consolidation.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a listless day weaker in low volumes, slipping below the psychologically important 3,800 level as early Wall Street lows put the market under pressure.
"We had a consolidation day after yesterday's record-breaking session", one dealer said, adding that U.S. CPI data had virtually no effect. Overall sentiment remained good.
"I think the market will target resistance at 3,820 points and head for 4,000 before the year's end", another trader said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 32.0 points, or 0.84 percent, at 3,790.2 points.
Broad SPI fell 0.65 percent, or 15.90 points, to 2,430.35.
An easing bond market also dampened sentiment.

Activity was high in pharmaceuticals. Actively-traded Roche fell 30 francs to 9,675 after a mostly higher bias throughout the session. Roche on Tuesday released better-than- expected sales figures for the first nine months of 1996.
Sandoz and Ciba suffered from sell orders by Geneva-based banks, yielding more than one percent each, a dealer said. Some switches into Roche also put pressure an the stocks.
Clariant, which said nine month sales rose five percent and confirmed earlier forcasts of double-digit net profit growth for full-year 1996, rose one franc to 445.

SMH bearer shares fell more than two percent, still pressured by last week's S&P Marketscope sell note following a review of the Smart Car project with Mercedes-Benz. One dealer said British investors were selling the stock, adding that recommendations may be reduced soon.
Banks and insurers were generally lower. UBS bearer shares fell eight francs to 1,248. CS Holding slid 1.37 percent.
Insurer Winterthur fell 1.15 percent to 775 after recent advances.
